subtitle: Look closely · follow the parts · play with words

sections.title: A rider-powered machine

beats.text: A bicycle is a wheeled vehicle.
The rider supplies the power by pushing the pedals.

sections.childPrompt: Find the two wheels and the two pedals.

sections.title: Every part helps in a different way
sections.visualLabel: A bicycle showing its main parts

beats.text: Wheels roll. Pedals are pushed by the rider's feet.
The handlebar helps the rider steer. Brakes help the bicycle slow down.
A bell and a carrier are useful additions, but not every bicycle has them.

sections.childPrompt: Point to a part, say its name, and tell what it helps the rider do.

sections.title: One action starts a chain

beats.text: Push pedals → crank turns → chain moves → rear wheel turns → bicycle moves.
Squeeze a brake lever → the brake engages → the bicycle slows.

sections.childPrompt: Trace each chain with your finger from the first action to the result.

sections.title: The same word can do two jobs
sections.visualLabel: A bicycle with its pedal area emphasised

beats.text: In “the pedal”, pedal names a part. In “pedal gently”, pedal names an action.
In “the brake”, brake names a part. In “brake before the turn”, brake names an action.

sections.childPrompt: Say one sentence where pedal names a part and another where it tells an action.

sections.title: Listen to the beginning and middle sounds
sections.visualLabel: A cat used for the short-a sound

beats.text: Cat, cap, and map share the short-a sound.
We say a bicycle and a helmet, but an apple. Listen to the opening sound.

sections.childPrompt: Say cat, cap, and map slowly. What sound stays the same?

sections.title: Use small clues from a sentence

beats.text: Ria fastens her helmet. She checks the brakes. Then she begins to pedal.
Words such as then and last help us follow the order. Actions help us work out simple reasons.

sections.childPrompt: What did Ria do first? What did she do last?

sections.title: Check the rider and the bicycle
sections.visualLabel: A bicycle, helmet, and safety check

beats.text: Fasten a properly fitted cycling helmet before riding.
Check that the brakes work and that the tyres are ready.
A bicycle bell can signal that a rider is nearby.

sections.childPrompt: Say the three checks before you begin: helmet, brakes, tyres.
